title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Values Equal to K
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the minimum operations needed to make all elements equal to k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the minimum operations needed to make all elements equal to k. An integer h is valid if all elements greater than h are equal. Operations involve setting elements greater than a valid h to h. Return -1 if it's impossible to make all elements equal to k.
constraints: An operation chooses a valid threshold and replaces every array value above it by that threshold.
A threshold is valid when every value strictly above it is equal.
Return the minimum operations to make all values k, or -1 if impossible.
hints: Values can only decrease, so any value below k makes the goal impossible.
Otherwise each distinct value above k must be removed as a level.
One valid operation eliminates exactly the current greatest remaining level.
Thus the number of distinct levels above k is both achievable and necessary.
editorial: Thus the number of distinct levels above k is both achievable and necessary.

tests.explanation: The distinct levels above two are five and four, requiring two operations.
A value below k can never be increased, so the target is impossible.
